Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk.001.name: Pulmonary trunk
Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk.001.description: The pulmonary trunk is the single large artery leaving the right ventricle. Unlike almost all other arteries, it carries oxygen-poor (deoxygenated) blood, which it sends to the lungs; it is about 5 cm long and 3 cm wide.

Right coronary artery.001.name: Right coronary artery
Right coronary artery.001.description: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the groove between the right atrium and right ventricle around to the back of the heart. In most people it also gives rise to the posterior descending artery.

Circumflex artery of heart.001.name: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
Circumflex artery of heart.001.description: The circumflex artery is one of the two main branches of the left main coronary artery and one of the three main coronary arteries. It curves to the left and around to the back of the heart.

Anterior interventricular artery.001.name: Anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery

Left coronary artery.001.name: Left coronary artery
Left coronary artery.001.description: The left coronary artery (left main) arises from the left aortic sinus just above the aortic valve. It is a short trunk, about 5-10 mm long, that passes behind the pulmonary trunk before dividing.

Right inferolateral branch of right coro.name: Right coronary artery
Right inferolateral branch of right coro.description: The right coronary artery arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the groove between the right atrium and right ventricle around to the back of the heart. In most people it also gives rise to the posterior descending artery.

Brachiocephalic trunk.001.name: Brachiocephalic trunk
Brachiocephalic trunk.001.description: The brachiocephalic trunk is the first and largest branch of the aortic arch. It is a short vessel, about 4-5 cm long, found only on the right side of the body.

Right common carotid artery.001.name: Common carotid artery
Right common carotid artery.001.description: The common carotid arteries are the main vessels running up each side of the neck. The right one branches from the brachiocephalic trunk while the left arises directly from the aortic arch.

Right subclavian artery.001.name: Subclavian artery
Right subclavian artery.001.description: The subclavian arteries run beneath the collarbones and are the main source of blood for the arms. The left arises directly from the aortic arch and the right from the brachiocephalic trunk.

Aortic arch.001.name: Arch of aorta
Aortic arch.001.description: The aortic arch is the curved segment that links the ascending aorta to the descending aorta. It bends upward, backward and to the left, giving the whole aorta its walking-cane shape.

Left common carotid artery.001.name: Common carotid artery
Left common carotid artery.001.description: The common carotid arteries are the main vessels running up each side of the neck. The right one branches from the brachiocephalic trunk while the left arises directly from the aortic arch.

Left subclavian artery.001.name: Subclavian artery
Left subclavian artery.001.description: The subclavian arteries run beneath the collarbones and are the main source of blood for the arms. The left arises directly from the aortic arch and the right from the brachiocephalic trunk.

Superior phrenic arteries.001.name: Thoracic aorta
Superior phrenic arteries.001.description: The thoracic (descending) aorta continues the arch down through the back of the chest, from T4 to the diaphragm. Its small superior phrenic branches to the top of the diaphragm are highlighted with it.

Thoracic aorta.001.name: Thoracic aorta
Thoracic aorta.001.description: The thoracic (descending) aorta continues the arch down through the back of the chest, from T4 to the diaphragm. Its small superior phrenic branches to the top of the diaphragm are highlighted with it.

Inferior suprarenal artery.l.001.name: Renal artery
Inferior suprarenal artery.l.001.description: The renal arteries are paired branches of the abdominal aorta that carry blood to the kidneys. Because the aorta lies left of the midline, the right renal artery is longer and passes behind the inferior vena cava.

Inferior phrenic artery.001.name: Inferior phrenic, lumbar and median sacral arteries
Inferior phrenic artery.001.description: These are the parietal (body wall) branches of the abdominal aorta. The inferior phrenic arteries are its first branches, the paired lumbar arteries arise from its back, and the small median sacral artery leaves near its bifurcation.

Lumbar arteries.l.001.description: These are the parietal (body wall) branches of the abdominal aorta. The inferior phrenic arteries are its first branches, the paired lumbar arteries arise from its back, and the small median sacral artery leaves near its bifurcation.

Splenic artery.001.name: Splenic artery
Splenic artery.001.description: The splenic artery is the largest branch of the coeliac trunk. It follows a winding (tortuous) course to the left along the upper border of the pancreas to reach the spleen.

Proper hepatic artery.001.name: Common hepatic, proper hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries
Proper hepatic artery.001.description: The common hepatic artery is the branch of the coeliac trunk that goes to the right. Near the duodenum it divides into the proper hepatic artery, which rises to the liver, and the gastroduodenal artery, which runs down behind the duodenum.

Coeliac trunk.001.name: Coeliac trunk
Coeliac trunk.001.description: The coeliac trunk is the first large unpaired branch of the abdominal aorta. It is a very short vessel, only about 1-2 cm long, that almost immediately divides into three arteries.

Left gastric artery.001.name: Left gastric artery
Left gastric artery.001.description: The left gastric artery is the smallest branch of the coeliac trunk. It rises toward the oesophagus and then runs along the lesser curvature of the stomach.

Common hepatic artery.001.name: Common hepatic, proper hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries
Common hepatic artery.001.description: The common hepatic artery is the branch of the coeliac trunk that goes to the right. Near the duodenum it divides into the proper hepatic artery, which rises to the liver, and the gastroduodenal artery, which runs down behind the duodenum.

Abdominal aorta.001.name: Abdominal aorta
Abdominal aorta.001.description: The abdominal aorta is the last part of the aorta, running about 13 cm from the diaphragm to the lower lumbar spine. It lies just in front of the vertebral bodies and ends by splitting into the two common iliac arteries.

Median sacral artery.001.name: Inferior phrenic, lumbar and median sacral arteries
Median sacral artery.001.description: These are the parietal (body wall) branches of the abdominal aorta. The inferior phrenic arteries are its first branches, the paired lumbar arteries arise from its back, and the small median sacral artery leaves near its bifurcation.

Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery.r.00.description: The internal iliac artery is the smaller terminal branch of the common iliac artery and the main artery of the pelvis. It dives into the pelvis and splits into anterior and posterior divisions.

Common iliac artery.r.001.description: The common iliac arteries are the two terminal branches of the abdominal aorta. Each runs down and outward toward the pelvis and divides into the internal and external iliac arteries.

Common iliac artery.l.001.name: Common iliac artery
Common iliac artery.l.001.description: The common iliac arteries are the two terminal branches of the abdominal aorta. Each runs down and outward toward the pelvis and divides into the internal and external iliac arteries.

Ascending aorta.001.name: Ascending aorta
Ascending aorta.001.description: The ascending aorta is the first segment of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle of the heart. It is roughly 5 cm long and sits inside the pericardial sac beside the pulmonary trunk.

Ascending pharyngeal artery.r.001.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery
Ascending pharyngeal artery.r.001.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is the smallest branch of the external carotid artery. It climbs straight up beside the throat toward the skull base.

Ascending pharyngeal artery.l.001.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is the smallest branch of the external carotid artery. It climbs straight up beside the throat toward the skull base.

Levator scapulae.r.001.description: The levator scapulae is a strap-like muscle running down the side and back of the neck. It arises from the transverse processes of C1-C4 and attaches to the upper medial border of the scapula.

Rhomboid major muscle.r.001.description: The rhomboids are two flat, parallel muscles between the spine and the shoulder blade. Rhomboid minor arises from C7-T1 and rhomboid major from T2-T5; both attach to the medial border of the scapula.

Levatores longi costarum.r.001.name: Levatores costarum muscles
Levatores longi costarum.r.001.description: The levatores costarum are twelve pairs of small muscles running from the transverse processes of C7-T11 to the rib below (breves) or two ribs below (longi).

Levatores breves costarum.r.001.name: Levatores costarum muscles
Levatores breves costarum.r.001.description: The levatores costarum are twelve pairs of small muscles running from the transverse processes of C7-T11 to the rib below (breves) or two ribs below (longi).

Pectoralis minor muscle.r.001.name: Pectoralis minor muscle
Pectoralis minor muscle.r.001.description: The pectoralis minor is a thin triangular muscle lying beneath pectoralis major. It arises from ribs 3-5 and attaches to the coracoid process of the scapula.

External intercostal muscles.r.001.name: Intercostal muscles
External intercostal muscles.r.001.description: The intercostal muscles fill the spaces between the ribs in three layers: external, internal and innermost. The external fibres run downward and forward, while the internal and innermost fibres run in roughly the opposite direction.

Internal intercostal muscles.r.001.name: Intercostal muscles
Internal intercostal muscles.r.001.description: The intercostal muscles fill the spaces between the ribs in three layers: external, internal and innermost. The external fibres run downward and forward, while the internal and innermost fibres run in roughly the opposite direction.

Serratus anterior muscle.r.001.name: Serratus anterior muscle
Serratus anterior muscle.r.001.description: The serratus anterior is a broad sheet of muscle wrapping around the side of the rib cage. It arises by finger-like slips from the upper ribs and attaches to the whole medial border of the scapula on its rib-facing side.

Innermost intercostal muscles.r.001.name: Intercostal muscles
Innermost intercostal muscles.r.001.description: The intercostal muscles fill the spaces between the ribs in three layers: external, internal and innermost. The external fibres run downward and forward, while the internal and innermost fibres run in roughly the opposite direction.

Subclavius muscle.r.001.name: Subclavius muscle
Subclavius muscle.r.001.description: The subclavius is a small, cylindrical muscle beneath the clavicle. It runs from the junction of the first rib and its cartilage to a groove on the underside of the middle clavicle.

Transversus thoracis muscle.r.001.name: Transversus thoracis muscle
Transversus thoracis muscle.r.001.description: The transversus thoracis is a thin sheet of muscle on the inside of the front chest wall. It runs from the back of the lower sternum and xiphoid process upward and outward to the costal cartilages of ribs 2-6.

External abdominal oblique muscle.r.001.name: External oblique muscle
External abdominal oblique muscle.r.001.description: The external oblique is the largest and most superficial of the three flat muscles of the side of the abdomen. It arises from ribs 5-12 and runs down and forward to the iliac crest, pubic tubercle and linea alba.

External abdominal oblique muscle.l.001.name: External oblique muscle
External abdominal oblique muscle.l.001.description: The external oblique is the largest and most superficial of the three flat muscles of the side of the abdomen. It arises from ribs 5-12 and runs down and forward to the iliac crest, pubic tubercle and linea alba.

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.r.001.name: Internal oblique muscle
Internal abdominal oblique muscle.r.001.description: The internal oblique is the middle layer of the flat abdominal muscles, lying beneath the external oblique. It arises from the inguinal ligament, iliac crest and thoracolumbar fascia and inserts on the lower ribs and linea alba.

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.l.001.name: Internal oblique muscle
Internal abdominal oblique muscle.l.001.description: The internal oblique is the middle layer of the flat abdominal muscles, lying beneath the external oblique. It arises from the inguinal ligament, iliac crest and thoracolumbar fascia and inserts on the lower ribs and linea alba.

Pyramidalis muscle.r.001.name: Pyramidalis muscle
Pyramidalis muscle.r.001.description: The pyramidalis is a small triangular muscle at the bottom of the front abdominal wall. It runs from the pubic crest to the linea alba, in front of the lower rectus abdominis.

Quadratus lumborum muscle.r.001.name: Quadratus lumborum muscle
Quadratus lumborum muscle.r.001.description: The quadratus lumborum is a thick, four-sided muscle of the posterior abdominal wall. It runs from the iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament up to the 12th rib and the transverse processes of L1-L4.

Quadratus lumborum muscle.l.001.description: The quadratus lumborum is a thick, four-sided muscle of the posterior abdominal wall. It runs from the iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament up to the 12th rib and the transverse processes of L1-L4.

Coccygeus muscle.r.001.name: Coccygeus muscle
Coccygeus muscle.r.001.description: The coccygeus is a triangular muscle and fibrous sheet at the back of the pelvic floor. It runs from the ischial spine to the edges of the lower sacrum and coccyx, overlying the sacrospinous ligament.

Acromial part of deltoid muscle.r.001.name: Deltoid muscle
Acromial part of deltoid muscle.r.001.description: The deltoid is the thick, triangular muscle that caps the shoulder and gives it its rounded outline. It has three parts - clavicular (front), acromial (middle) and spinal (back) - that converge on the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus.

Subscapularis muscle.r.001.name: Subscapularis muscle
Subscapularis muscle.r.001.description: The subscapularis is the rotator cuff muscle on the front (rib-facing) surface of the scapula. Its tendon crosses in front of the shoulder joint to the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

Supraspinatus muscle.r.001.name: Supraspinatus muscle
Supraspinatus muscle.r.001.description: The supraspinatus is a rotator cuff muscle that fills the supraspinous fossa above the spine of the scapula. Its tendon passes under the acromion to the top of the greater tubercle of the humerus.

Teres minor muscle.r.001.name: Teres minor muscle
Teres minor muscle.r.001.description: The teres minor is a narrow rotator cuff muscle running from the lateral border of the back of the scapula to the greater tubercle of the humerus. It lies just below infraspinatus.

Infraspinatus muscle.r.001.name: Infraspinatus muscle
Infraspinatus muscle.r.001.description: The infraspinatus is a thick triangular rotator cuff muscle occupying most of the infraspinous fossa below the spine of the scapula. Its tendon attaches to the greater tubercle of the humerus.

Coracobrachialis muscle.r.001.name: Coracobrachialis muscle
Coracobrachialis muscle.r.001.description: The coracobrachialis is a slim muscle of the front compartment of the arm. It arises from the tip of the coracoid process alongside the short head of biceps and inserts on the middle of the inner shaft of the humerus.

Superficial head of pronator teres.r.001.description: The pronator teres is a two-headed muscle crossing the upper forearm obliquely from the medial epicondyle and the coronoid process of the ulna to the middle of the radius.

Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle
Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.description: The flexor digitorum superficialis is a broad muscle in the middle layer of the front of the forearm. It has humero-ulnar and radial heads and sends four tendons through the carpal tunnel to the middle phalanges of the fingers.

Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle
Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum su.description: The flexor digitorum superficialis is a broad muscle in the middle layer of the front of the forearm. It has humero-ulnar and radial heads and sends four tendons through the carpal tunnel to the middle phalanges of the fingers.

Flexor carpi radialis.r.001.name: Flexor carpi radialis muscle
Flexor carpi radialis.r.001.description: The flexor carpi radialis is a superficial muscle of the front of the forearm. It arises from the medial epicondyle through the common flexor tendon and its tendon ends on the bases of the second and third metacarpals.

Palmaris longus muscle.r.001.name: Palmaris longus muscle
Palmaris longus muscle.r.001.description: The palmaris longus is a small, slender muscle of the front of the forearm with a long thin tendon. It runs from the medial epicondyle to the flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis.

Flexor carpi radialis.l.001.name: Flexor carpi radialis muscle
Flexor carpi radialis.l.001.description: The flexor carpi radialis is a superficial muscle of the front of the forearm. It arises from the medial epicondyle through the common flexor tendon and its tendon ends on the bases of the second and third metacarpals.

Palmaris longus muscle.l.001.name: Palmaris longus muscle
Palmaris longus muscle.l.001.description: The palmaris longus is a small, slender muscle of the front of the forearm with a long thin tendon. It runs from the medial epicondyle to the flexor retinaculum and palmar aponeurosis.

Radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle
Radial head of flexor digitorum superfic.description: The flexor digitorum superficialis is a broad muscle in the middle layer of the front of the forearm. It has humero-ulnar and radial heads and sends four tendons through the carpal tunnel to the middle phalanges of the fingers.

Flexor digitorum profundus.r.001.name: Flexor digitorum profundus muscle
Flexor digitorum profundus.r.001.description: The flexor digitorum profundus is a deep forearm muscle arising from the ulna and interosseous membrane. Its four tendons pass through the carpal tunnel and through the split superficialis tendons to reach the fingertips.

Flexor pollicis longus.r.001.name: Flexor pollicis longus muscle
Flexor pollicis longus.r.001.description: The flexor pollicis longus is a deep muscle of the front of the forearm. It arises from the front of the radius and the interosseous membrane and its tendon passes through the carpal tunnel to the distal phalanx of the thumb.

Pronator quadratus.r.001.name: Pronator quadratus muscle
Pronator quadratus.r.001.description: The pronator quadratus is a flat, square muscle stretching across the lower front of the forearm between the ulna and the radius.

Extensor digitorum.r.001.name: Extensor digitorum muscle
Extensor digitorum.r.001.description: The extensor digitorum is the main finger-straightening muscle on the back of the forearm. It arises from the lateral epicondyle through the common extensor tendon and divides into four tendons to the index to little fingers.

Extensor digitorum.l.001.name: Extensor digitorum muscle
Extensor digitorum.l.001.description: The extensor digitorum is the main finger-straightening muscle on the back of the forearm. It arises from the lateral epicondyle through the common extensor tendon and divides into four tendons to the index to little fingers.

Brachioradialis muscle.r.001.name: Brachioradialis muscle
Brachioradialis muscle.r.001.description: The brachioradialis is a superficial muscle on the thumb side of the forearm. It runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus to the lower end of the radius near the styloid process.

Extensor carpi radialis longus.r.001.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus muscle
Extensor carpi radialis longus.r.001.description: The extensor carpi radialis longus is a superficial muscle of the back-outer forearm. It arises from the lower lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus and its tendon ends on the back of the base of the second metacarpal.

Extensor carpi radialis brevis.r.001.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle
Extensor carpi radialis brevis.r.001.description: The extensor carpi radialis brevis is a wrist extensor that lies just behind the longus. It arises from the lateral epicondyle through the common extensor tendon and ends on the back of the base of the third metacarpal.

Anconeus muscle.r.001.name: Anconeus muscle
Anconeus muscle.r.001.description: The anconeus is a small triangular muscle at the back of the elbow. It runs from the back of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus to the outer side of the olecranon and upper ulna.

Extensor digiti minimi.r.001.name: Extensor digiti minimi muscle
Extensor digiti minimi.r.001.description: The extensor digiti minimi is a slender muscle that is often partly joined to extensor digitorum. It arises from the lateral epicondyle and its tendon joins the extensor expansion of the little finger.

Brachioradialis muscle.l.001.name: Brachioradialis muscle

Anconeus muscle.l.001.name: Anconeus muscle

Extensor digiti minimi.l.001.name: Extensor digiti minimi muscle
Extensor digiti minimi.l.001.description: The extensor digiti minimi is a slender muscle that is often partly joined to extensor digitorum. It arises from the lateral epicondyle and its tendon joins the extensor expansion of the little finger.

Supinator.r.001.name: Supinator muscle
Supinator.r.001.description: The supinator is a broad, curved muscle wrapped around the upper radius. It arises from the lateral epicondyle, the ligaments of the elbow and the supinator crest of the ulna and winds around to the upper shaft of the radius.

Gluteus medius muscle.r.001.name: Gluteus medius muscle
Gluteus medius muscle.r.001.description: The gluteus medius is a broad, fan-shaped muscle on the outer surface of the ilium, partly hidden under the gluteus maximus. Its fibres converge on the outer side of the greater trochanter of the femur.

Gluteus maximus muscle.r.001.name: Gluteus maximus muscle
Gluteus maximus muscle.r.001.description: The gluteus maximus is the thick, superficial muscle that gives the buttock its shape. It arises from the back of the ilium, the sacrum and the coccyx and ends partly on the femur and partly in the iliotibial tract.

Gluteus minimus muscle.r.001.name: Gluteus minimus muscle
Gluteus minimus muscle.r.001.description: The gluteus minimus is the smallest and deepest of the three gluteal muscles. It is a fan-shaped muscle that arises from the outer surface of the ilium, beneath gluteus medius, and attaches to the front of the greater trochanter.

Tensor fasciae latae.r.001.name: Tensor fasciae latae muscle
Tensor fasciae latae.r.001.description: The tensor fasciae latae is a small muscle at the front-outer corner of the hip, enclosed within the deep fascia of the thigh. It pulls on the iliotibial tract, which carries its force down to the knee.

Gluteus medius muscle.l.001.name: Gluteus medius muscle
Gluteus medius muscle.l.001.description: The gluteus medius is a broad, fan-shaped muscle on the outer surface of the ilium, partly hidden under the gluteus maximus. Its fibres converge on the outer side of the greater trochanter of the femur.

Gluteus maximus muscle.l.001.name: Gluteus maximus muscle
Gluteus maximus muscle.l.001.description: The gluteus maximus is the thick, superficial muscle that gives the buttock its shape. It arises from the back of the ilium, the sacrum and the coccyx and ends partly on the femur and partly in the iliotibial tract.

Gluteus minimus muscle.l.001.name: Gluteus minimus muscle
Gluteus minimus muscle.l.001.description: The gluteus minimus is the smallest and deepest of the three gluteal muscles. It is a fan-shaped muscle that arises from the outer surface of the ilium, beneath gluteus medius, and attaches to the front of the greater trochanter.

Tensor fasciae latae.l.001.name: Tensor fasciae latae muscle
Tensor fasciae latae.l.001.description: The tensor fasciae latae is a small muscle at the front-outer corner of the hip, enclosed within the deep fascia of the thigh. It pulls on the iliotibial tract, which carries its force down to the knee.

Piriformis muscle.r.001.name: Piriformis muscle
Piriformis muscle.r.001.description: The piriformis is a flat, pear-shaped muscle that runs from the front of the sacrum, through the greater sciatic foramen, to the greater trochanter of the femur. It is one of the small deep rotators of the hip.

Rectus femoris muscle.r.001.name: Rectus femoris muscle
Rectus femoris muscle.r.001.description: The rectus femoris is the central, superficial head of the quadriceps femoris. Unlike the three vastus muscles, it starts on the pelvis rather than the femur.

Vastus lateralis muscle.r.001.name: Vastus lateralis muscle
Vastus lateralis muscle.r.001.description: The vastus lateralis is the outer head of the quadriceps femoris. It arises from a long strip of the femur, including the greater trochanter and the linea aspera, and joins the quadriceps tendon above the patella.

Vastus medialis muscle.r.001.name: Vastus medialis muscle
Vastus medialis muscle.r.001.description: The vastus medialis is the inner head of the quadriceps femoris, arising from the medial side of the femur. Its lowest, obliquely running fibres form a visible 'teardrop' just above and inside the knee.

Vastus intermedius muscle.r.001.name: Vastus intermedius muscle
Vastus intermedius muscle.r.001.description: The vastus intermedius is the deepest head of the quadriceps femoris, lying directly on the front of the femur beneath the rectus femoris. It blends with the other heads into the quadriceps tendon.

Rectus femoris muscle.l.001.name: Rectus femoris muscle
Rectus femoris muscle.l.001.description: The rectus femoris is the central, superficial head of the quadriceps femoris. Unlike the three vastus muscles, it starts on the pelvis rather than the femur.

Vastus medialis muscle.l.001.description: The vastus medialis is the inner head of the quadriceps femoris, arising from the medial side of the femur. Its lowest, obliquely running fibres form a visible 'teardrop' just above and inside the knee.

Vastus intermedius muscle.l.001.name: Vastus intermedius muscle
Vastus intermedius muscle.l.001.description: The vastus intermedius is the deepest head of the quadriceps femoris, lying directly on the front of the femur beneath the rectus femoris. It blends with the other heads into the quadriceps tendon.

Sartorius muscle.r.001.name: Sartorius muscle
Sartorius muscle.r.001.description: The sartorius is a thin, strap-like muscle that crosses the front of the thigh diagonally from the hip to the inner side of the knee. It crosses both the hip and the knee joints.

Sartorius muscle.l.001.name: Sartorius muscle
Sartorius muscle.l.001.description: The sartorius is a thin, strap-like muscle that crosses the front of the thigh diagonally from the hip to the inner side of the knee. It crosses both the hip and the knee joints.

Adductor magnus.r.001.name: Adductor magnus muscle
Adductor magnus.r.001.description: The adductor magnus is the largest muscle of the inner thigh and has two parts: an adductor part from the pubic and ischial rami and a 'hamstring' part from the ischial tuberosity. Its upper fibres are sometimes described separately as…

Adductor longus.r.001.name: Adductor longus muscle
Adductor longus.r.001.description: The adductor longus is a flat, fan-shaped muscle of the inner thigh. It arises from the body of the pubis and spreads out to the middle third of the linea aspera on the back of the femur.

Pectineus muscle.r.001.name: Pectineus muscle
Pectineus muscle.r.001.description: The pectineus is a flat, four-sided muscle at the top of the inner thigh. It runs from the pectineal line of the pubis down to the pectineal line on the back of the upper femur, just below the lesser trochanter.

Adductor brevis.r.001.name: Adductor brevis muscle
Adductor brevis.r.001.description: The adductor brevis is a short, triangular adductor that lies behind pectineus and adductor longus. It arises from the body and inferior ramus of the pubis and attaches to the upper part of the linea aspera of the femur.

Gracilis muscle.r.001.name: Gracilis muscle
Gracilis muscle.r.001.description: The gracilis is a long, slender muscle that is the most superficial and medial of the thigh adductors. It runs from the pubis to the upper medial tibia.

Long head of biceps femoris.r.001.name: Biceps femoris muscle
Long head of biceps femoris.r.001.description: The biceps femoris is the lateral hamstring muscle. Its long head arises from the ischial tuberosity and its short head from the linea aspera of the femur; both join to insert on the head of the fibula.

Short head of biceps femoris.r.001.name: Biceps femoris muscle
Short head of biceps femoris.r.001.description: The biceps femoris is the lateral hamstring muscle. Its long head arises from the ischial tuberosity and its short head from the linea aspera of the femur; both join to insert on the head of the fibula.

Short head of biceps femoris.l.001.name: Biceps femoris muscle

Semimembranosus muscle.r.001.name: Semimembranosus muscle
Semimembranosus muscle.r.001.description: The semimembranosus is a broad, flat hamstring muscle named for its flat, membrane-like tendon of origin. It runs from the ischial tuberosity to the back of the medial tibial condyle.

Semitendinosus muscle.r.001.name: Semitendinosus muscle
Semitendinosus muscle.r.001.description: The semitendinosus is a medial hamstring that is fleshy above and continues as a long, cord-like tendon below. It runs from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial surface of the tibia.

Semimembranosus muscle.l.001.name: Semimembranosus muscle

Semitendinosus muscle.l.001.name: Semitendinosus muscle
Semitendinosus muscle.l.001.description: The semitendinosus is a medial hamstring that is fleshy above and continues as a long, cord-like tendon below. It runs from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial surface of the tibia.

Extensor digitorum longus.r.001.description: The extensor digitorum longus is a feather-shaped muscle on the front-outer side of the leg. It arises from the lateral tibial condyle, the fibula and the interosseous membrane, and its tendon splits into four slips to the second to fifth…

Tibialis anterior muscle.r.001.name: Tibialis anterior muscle
Tibialis anterior muscle.r.001.description: The tibialis anterior is the main muscle at the front of the leg, lying just lateral to the shin bone. It is fleshy above and becomes a strong tendon that crosses the front of the ankle.

Fibularis tertius muscle.r.001.name: Fibularis tertius muscle
Fibularis tertius muscle.r.001.description: The fibularis tertius is a small muscle of the front of the leg that is usually a separated lower part of extensor digitorum longus. It runs from the lower fibula to the back (dorsal surface) of the base of the fifth metatarsal.

Extensor hallucis longus.r.001.name: Extensor hallucis longus muscle
Extensor hallucis longus.r.001.description: The extensor hallucis longus is a thin muscle of the front of the leg, lying between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus. It arises from the middle fibula and interosseous membrane and inserts on the base of the distal phalanx…

Tibialis anterior muscle.l.001.name: Tibialis anterior muscle
Tibialis anterior muscle.l.001.description: The tibialis anterior is the main muscle at the front of the leg, lying just lateral to the shin bone. It is fleshy above and becomes a strong tendon that crosses the front of the ankle.

Fibularis longus muscle.r.001.name: Fibularis longus muscle
Fibularis longus muscle.r.001.description: The fibularis (peroneus) longus is the superficial muscle of the lateral compartment of the leg. Its tendon passes behind the lateral malleolus and then crosses the sole of the foot.

Fibularis brevis muscle.r.001.name: Fibularis brevis muscle
Fibularis brevis muscle.r.001.description: The fibularis (peroneus) brevis is the shorter of the two lateral compartment muscles of the leg. It arises from the lower two-thirds of the outer fibula and its tendon passes behind the lateral malleolus to the base of the fifth…

Lateral head of gastrocnemius.r.001.name: Gastrocnemius muscle
Lateral head of gastrocnemius.r.001.description: The gastrocnemius is the superficial two-headed muscle that forms the visible bulge of the calf. Its heads arise from the femoral condyles and join the soleus to form the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

Medial head of gastrocnemius.r.001.name: Gastrocnemius muscle
Medial head of gastrocnemius.r.001.description: The gastrocnemius is the superficial two-headed muscle that forms the visible bulge of the calf. Its heads arise from the femoral condyles and join the soleus to form the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

Calcaneal tendon.r.001.name: Calcaneal tendon
Calcaneal tendon.r.001.description: The calcaneal tendon is the shared tendon of the gastrocnemius and soleus (the triceps surae). It attaches to the back of the heel bone (calcaneus).

Lateral head of gastrocnemius.l.001.name: Gastrocnemius muscle
Lateral head of gastrocnemius.l.001.description: The gastrocnemius is the superficial two-headed muscle that forms the visible bulge of the calf. Its heads arise from the femoral condyles and join the soleus to form the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

Medial head of gastrocnemius.l.001.name: Gastrocnemius muscle
Medial head of gastrocnemius.l.001.description: The gastrocnemius is the superficial two-headed muscle that forms the visible bulge of the calf. Its heads arise from the femoral condyles and join the soleus to form the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

Calcaneal tendon.l.001.name: Calcaneal tendon
Calcaneal tendon.l.001.description: The calcaneal tendon is the shared tendon of the gastrocnemius and soleus (the triceps surae). It attaches to the back of the heel bone (calcaneus).

Soleus muscle.r.001.name: Soleus muscle
Soleus muscle.r.001.description: The soleus is a broad, flat calf muscle lying beneath the gastrocnemius; together they form the superficial layer of the back of the leg. It arises from the back of the upper tibia (soleal line) and fibula and joins the calcaneal tendon.

Soleus muscle.l.001.name: Soleus muscle
Soleus muscle.l.001.description: The soleus is a broad, flat calf muscle lying beneath the gastrocnemius; together they form the superficial layer of the back of the leg. It arises from the back of the upper tibia (soleal line) and fibula and joins the calcaneal tendon.

Plantaris muscle.r.001.name: Plantaris muscle
Plantaris muscle.r.001.description: The plantaris is a small muscle with a short belly and a very long, thin tendon. It arises just above the lateral femoral condyle and its tendon runs between gastrocnemius and soleus to join the calcaneal tendon or the heel.

Plantaris muscle.l.001.name: Plantaris muscle
Plantaris muscle.l.001.description: The plantaris is a small muscle with a short belly and a very long, thin tendon. It arises just above the lateral femoral condyle and its tendon runs between gastrocnemius and soleus to join the calcaneal tendon or the heel.

Flexor digitorum longus.r.001.name: Flexor digitorum longus muscle
Flexor digitorum longus.r.001.description: The flexor digitorum longus is a deep muscle on the tibial side of the back of the leg. It arises from the back of the tibia and its tendon passes behind the medial malleolus, then splits in the sole into four tendons to the distal…

Popliteus muscle.r.001.name: Popliteus muscle
Popliteus muscle.r.001.description: The popliteus is a thin, triangular muscle at the back of the knee. It runs from the outer side of the lateral femoral condyle, inside the joint capsule, to the back of the upper tibia above the soleal line.

Tibialis posterior muscle.r.001.name: Tibialis posterior muscle
Tibialis posterior muscle.r.001.description: The tibialis posterior is the deepest muscle of the back of the leg, lying on the interosseous membrane between tibia and fibula. Its tendon passes behind the medial malleolus to the navicular and other tarsal bones.

Flexor hallucis longus.r.001.name: Flexor hallucis longus muscle
Flexor hallucis longus.r.001.description: The flexor hallucis longus is a strong muscle of the deep back of the leg. It arises from the lower two-thirds of the back of the fibula and its tendon runs behind the medial malleolus and under the sole to the distal phalanx of the big…

Popliteus muscle.l.001.name: Popliteus muscle
Popliteus muscle.l.001.description: The popliteus is a thin, triangular muscle at the back of the knee. It runs from the outer side of the lateral femoral condyle, inside the joint capsule, to the back of the upper tibia above the soleal line.

Tibialis posterior muscle.l.001.name: Tibialis posterior muscle
Tibialis posterior muscle.l.001.description: The tibialis posterior is the deepest muscle of the back of the leg, lying on the interosseous membrane between tibia and fibula. Its tendon passes behind the medial malleolus to the navicular and other tarsal bones.

Iliotibial tract.r.001.name: Iliotibial tract
Iliotibial tract.r.001.description: The iliotibial tract is a long, thick band of fibrous tissue that is a reinforced part of the fascia lata, the deep fascia of the thigh. It is not a muscle itself but acts as a tendon for tensor fasciae latae and part of gluteus maximus.

External anal sphincter.r.001.name: External anal sphincter
External anal sphincter.r.001.description: The external anal sphincter is a ring of skeletal muscle surrounding the lower anal canal. It is described as having subcutaneous, superficial and deep parts and blends above with the puborectalis part of levator ani.

Dorsal scapular nerve.r.001.description: A small motor nerve that comes straight off the C5 root of the brachial plexus, pierces the middle scalene muscle and runs down the inner edge of the shoulder blade.

Long thoracic nerve.r.001.description: A motor nerve that arises directly from the C5, C6 and C7 roots of the brachial plexus and runs down the side of the chest wall. It is the only nerve supply of the serratus anterior muscle.

Suprascapular nerve.r.001.name: Suprascapular nerve

Subclavian nerve.r.001.name: Nerve to subclavius (subclavian nerve)

Spleen.001.description: The spleen is the largest lymphoid organ, a soft, fist-sized, purple organ with a thin capsule. Inside, red pulp filters the blood and white pulp contains lymphocytes arranged around small arteries. Vessels enter and leave at its hilum on…

Parietal bone.r.001.name: Parietal bone
Parietal bone.r.001.description: A paired, roughly four-sided curved plate of bone. The two parietal bones meet in the midline at the sagittal suture and together form most of the roof and upper sides of the braincase.

Parietal bone.l.001.name: Parietal bone
Parietal bone.l.001.description: A paired, roughly four-sided curved plate of bone. The two parietal bones meet in the midline at the sagittal suture and together form most of the roof and upper sides of the braincase.

Sinus of frontal bone.001.name: Frontal sinus
Sinus of frontal bone.001.description: An air-filled space lined with mucous membrane inside the frontal bone, behind the brow. It is one of the four pairs of paranasal sinuses; the left and right sides are split by a thin bony wall and are often unequal in size. The maxillary…

Frontal bone.001.name: Frontal bone
Frontal bone.001.description: A single, shell-shaped flat bone that forms the forehead and the front of the braincase. Its vertical squamous part makes the forehead, while its horizontal orbital plates form most of the roofs of the eye sockets and the floor of the…

Occipital bone.001.name: Occipital bone
Occipital bone.001.description: A single, dish-shaped bone that forms the back and much of the base of the skull. It contains the foramen magnum, the large opening through which the brainstem continues as the spinal cord.

Sinus of sphenoid bone.001.name: Sphenoidal sinus
Sinus of sphenoid bone.001.description: An air-filled space lined with mucous membrane inside the body of the sphenoid bone, usually divided into left and right parts by a thin septum. It is the deepest of the paranasal sinuses.

Sphenoid bone.001.name: Sphenoid bone
Sphenoid bone.001.description: An unpaired, winged bone at the centre of the skull base, made of a body, greater and lesser wings and downward pterygoid processes. The top of its body forms the sella turcica, a saddle-shaped seat for the pituitary gland.

Temporal bone.r.001.name: Temporal bone
Temporal bone.r.001.description: A complex paired bone at the side and base of the skull made of squamous, mastoid, petrous and tympanic parts. It contains the ear canal, middle ear and inner ear, and has a socket for the lower jaw.

Ethmoid bone.001.name: Ethmoid bone
Ethmoid bone.001.description: A light, spongy, unpaired bone that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. It has a horizontal cribriform plate, a vertical perpendicular plate and two labyrinths full of air cells.

Inferior nasal concha bone.r.001.name: Inferior nasal concha
Inferior nasal concha bone.r.001.description: A thin, curled, scroll-like bone on the side wall of each nasal cavity. Unlike the superior and middle conchae, which belong to the ethmoid, it is a separate facial bone.

Lacrimal bone.r.001.name: Lacrimal bone
Lacrimal bone.r.001.description: A small, thin, fragile paired bone in the inner wall of the eye socket. It holds a groove for the lacrimal sac, part of the tear drainage system.

Nasal bone.r.001.name: Nasal bone
Nasal bone.r.001.description: Two small oblong bones that meet in the midline to form the bony bridge of the nose. The rest of the external nose is shaped by cartilage attached to their lower edges.

Maxilla.r.001.name: Maxilla
Maxilla.r.001.description: A paired, pyramid-shaped bone of the midface; the two maxillae fuse to form the upper jaw. It has a hollow body containing the maxillary sinus and four processes: zygomatic, frontal, palatine and alveolar.

Palatine bone.r.001.name: Palatine bone
Palatine bone.r.001.description: A paired, L-shaped bone with horizontal and perpendicular plates. The horizontal plates form the back part of the hard palate, behind the maxillae.

Zygomatic bone.r.001.name: Zygomatic bone
Zygomatic bone.r.001.description: A paired, irregular bone that forms the prominence of the cheek and the outer rim of the eye socket. Its temporal process joins the temporal bone to form the zygomatic arch.

Mandible.001.name: Mandible
Mandible.001.description: The largest and strongest bone of the face, made of a horseshoe-shaped body and two upright rami. It holds the lower teeth and is the only skull bone connected to the rest of the skull by a freely movable joint (the temporomandibular…

Hyoid bone.001.name: Hyoid bone
Hyoid bone.001.description: A small U-shaped bone in the front of the neck with a body and two pairs of horns. It does not form a joint with any other bone; muscles and ligaments hold it in place.

Malleus.r.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Malleus.r.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Incus.r.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Incus.r.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Stapes.r.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Stapes.r.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Upper medial incisor.r.001.name: Incisor teeth
Upper medial incisor.r.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Upper lateral incisor.r.001.name: Incisor teeth
Upper lateral incisor.r.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Upper canine.r.001.name: Canine teeth
Upper canine.r.001.description: Four pointed, cone-shaped teeth, one at each corner of the dental arches. Each has a single, very long root anchored deep in the jaw.

Lower medial incisor.r.001.name: Incisor teeth
Lower medial incisor.r.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Lower lateral incisor.r.001.name: Incisor teeth
Lower lateral incisor.r.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Lower canine.r.001.name: Canine teeth
Lower canine.r.001.description: Four pointed, cone-shaped teeth, one at each corner of the dental arches. Each has a single, very long root anchored deep in the jaw.

Upper first premolar.r.001.name: Premolar teeth
Upper first premolar.r.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Upper second premolar.r.001.name: Premolar teeth
Upper second premolar.r.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Upper first molar tooth.r.001.name: Molar teeth
Upper first molar tooth.r.001.description: The large, broad teeth at the back of the mouth, with several cusps and multiple roots: usually three in upper molars and two in lower molars. Adults normally have 12 molars including the wisdom teeth; this model shows the first and second…

Major alar cartilage.r.001.description: The flexible cartilage framework of the lower external nose. The roughly four-sided septal cartilage divides the nostrils, its lateral processes (commonly called the upper lateral cartilages) form the sides of the middle part of the nose…

Thyroid cartilage.001.name: Thyroid cartilage
Thyroid cartilage.001.description: The largest cartilage of the larynx, made of two plates that join at the front in a ridge called the laryngeal prominence. The prominence is more pronounced in men because the larynx enlarges under testosterone at puberty.

Cricoid cartilage.001.name: Cricoid cartilage
Cricoid cartilage.001.description: A signet-ring-shaped cartilage forming the base of the larynx, with a narrow arch at the front and a broad plate (lamina) at the back. It is the only complete ring of cartilage around the airway.

Arytenoid cartilage.r.001.name: Arytenoid and corniculate cartilages
Arytenoid cartilage.r.001.description: A pair of small, three-sided pyramid-shaped cartilages sitting on the back of the cricoid, each capped by a tiny horn-like corniculate cartilage. The vocal cords attach to their forward-pointing vocal processes.

Corniculate cartilage.r.001.name: Arytenoid and corniculate cartilages
Corniculate cartilage.r.001.description: A pair of small, three-sided pyramid-shaped cartilages sitting on the back of the cricoid, each capped by a tiny horn-like corniculate cartilage. The vocal cords attach to their forward-pointing vocal processes.

Atlas (C1).001.name: Atlas (first cervical vertebra, C1)
Atlas (C1).001.description: The first neck vertebra, a ring of bone with front and back arches and two lateral masses but no vertebral body. Its upper surfaces cradle the occipital condyles of the skull.

Vertebra C6.001.name: Cervical vertebrae C3-C7
Vertebra C6.001.description: The lower five of the seven neck vertebrae. They are small, with a triangular vertebral foramen, a hole in each transverse process (transverse foramen) and, in C3-C6, a split (bifid) spinous process.

Vertebra C3.001.description: The lower five of the seven neck vertebrae. They are small, with a triangular vertebral foramen, a hole in each transverse process (transverse foramen) and, in C3-C6, a split (bifid) spinous process.

Vertebra T2.001.name: Thoracic vertebrae T1-T12
Vertebra T2.001.description: Twelve medium-sized vertebrae with heart-shaped bodies, facets on their sides for the heads of the ribs, and long spinous processes that slope steeply downward.

Vertebra L1.001.name: Lumbar vertebrae L1-L5
Vertebra L1.001.description: Five large vertebrae with thick, kidney-shaped bodies and short, broad spinous processes. They lack the transverse foramina of neck vertebrae and the rib facets of thoracic vertebrae.

Vertebra L2.001.description: Five large vertebrae with thick, kidney-shaped bodies and short, broad spinous processes. They lack the transverse foramina of neck vertebrae and the rib facets of thoracic vertebrae.

Coccyx.001.name: Coccyx
Coccyx.001.description: The small last segment of the spine, made of three to five (most often four) tiny fused coccygeal vertebrae. It is an evolutionary remnant of a tail.

Fifth rib.r.001.name: True ribs (ribs 1-7)
Fifth rib.r.001.description: The first seven pairs of ribs, each joined directly to the sternum by its own costal cartilage. A typical rib has a head, neck, tubercle and curved body (shaft), with a costal groove underneath for the intercostal nerve and vessels.

First rib.r.001.description: The first seven pairs of ribs, each joined directly to the sternum by its own costal cartilage. A typical rib has a head, neck, tubercle and curved body (shaft), with a costal groove underneath for the intercostal nerve and vessels.

Eleventh rib.r.001.name: Floating ribs (ribs 11-12)
Eleventh rib.r.001.description: The last two pairs of ribs, which attach only to the vertebrae at the back and end freely in the muscles of the abdominal wall. Ribs 11 and 12 are the lowest of the false ribs. They are short and have no neck or tubercle.

Twelfth rib.r.001.name: Floating ribs (ribs 11-12)
Twelfth rib.r.001.description: The last two pairs of ribs, which attach only to the vertebrae at the back and end freely in the muscles of the abdominal wall. Ribs 11 and 12 are the lowest of the false ribs. They are short and have no neck or tubercle.

Eighth rib.r.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Eighth rib.r.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Ninth rib.r.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Ninth rib.r.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Tenth rib.r.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Tenth rib.r.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Manubrium of sternum.001.name: Manubrium of sternum
Manubrium of sternum.001.description: The broad upper part of the sternum. Its upper edge forms the jugular (suprasternal) notch, and its sides join the clavicles and the first ribs.

Xiphoid process.001.name: Xiphoid process
Xiphoid process.001.description: The small, pointed lower tip of the sternum. It is mostly cartilage in young people and gradually turns to bone.

Body of sternum.001.name: Body of sternum
Body of sternum.001.description: The long, flat middle part of the sternum, also called the gladiolus. Its edges have notches where the costal cartilages of ribs 2 to 7 attach.

Costal cartilage of first rib.r.001.name: Costal cartilages
Costal cartilage of first rib.r.001.description: Bars of hyaline cartilage that extend the front ends of the ribs. The first seven join the sternum directly, while those of ribs 8-10 join the cartilage above.

Clavicle.r.001.name: Clavicle
Clavicle.r.001.description: A slender S-shaped long bone, about 15 cm long, that lies horizontally at the base of the neck. Its inner end joins the sternum and its outer end joins the acromion of the scapula.

Humerus.r.001.name: Humerus
Humerus.r.001.description: The long bone of the upper arm. Its rounded head fits into the scapula's glenoid cavity, and its lower end carries the trochlea and capitulum, which meet the ulna and radius at the elbow.

Patella.r.001.name: Patella
Patella.r.001.description: A flat, rounded triangular bone set inside the quadriceps tendon at the front of the knee. Its back surface is covered with thick cartilage where it glides on the femur.

Talus.r.001.name: Talus
Talus.r.001.description: The tarsal bone at the top of the foot skeleton, gripped between the tibia and fibula at the ankle joint and resting on the calcaneus. Much of its surface is covered in joint cartilage.

Calcaneus.r.001.name: Calcaneus
Calcaneus.r.001.description: The largest tarsal bone, forming the heel. Its back part, the calcaneal tuberosity, receives the Achilles tendon, and a shelf on its inner side (sustentaculum tali) supports the talus.

Navicular bone.r.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Navicular bone.r.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Cuboid bone.r.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Cuboid bone.r.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Intermediate cuneiform bone.r.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Intermediate cuneiform bone.r.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Lateral cuneiform bone.r.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Lateral cuneiform bone.r.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Medial cuneiform bone.r.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Medial cuneiform bone.r.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

First metatarsal bone.r.001.name: Metatarsal bones
First metatarsal bone.r.001.description: Five long bones numbered I to V from the big-toe side. Each has a base joining the tarsals, a shaft, and a head that meets a toe.

Fifth metatarsal bone.r.001.name: Metatarsal bones

Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r.name: Phalanges of foot
Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot.r.description: Fourteen small bones in each foot: three in each of the lesser toes and two (proximal and distal) in the big toe.

Sesamoid bones of foot.r.001.name: Sesamoid bones of foot
Sesamoid bones of foot.r.001.description: Small pea-like bones embedded in tendons. In the foot there are usually two under the head of the first metatarsal, inside the tendons of flexor hallucis brevis.

Distal phalanx of first finger of hand.r.name: Phalanges of hand
Distal phalanx of first finger of hand.r.description: Fourteen small long bones in each hand: three (proximal, middle, distal) in each finger and two in the thumb. The distal phalanges end in flattened tufts that support the fingertip pad and nail.

First metacarpal bone.r.001.name: Metacarpal bones
First metacarpal bone.r.001.description: Five long bones in the palm, numbered I (thumb) to V (little finger). Each has a base joining the carpals, a shaft, and a head that forms a knuckle.

Second metacarpal bone.r.001.name: Metacarpal bones
Second metacarpal bone.r.001.description: Five long bones in the palm, numbered I (thumb) to V (little finger). Each has a base joining the carpals, a shaft, and a head that forms a knuckle.

Fifth metacarpal bone.r.001.description: Five long bones in the palm, numbered I (thumb) to V (little finger). Each has a base joining the carpals, a shaft, and a head that forms a knuckle.

Capitate bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Capitate bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Hamate bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Hamate bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Lunate bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Lunate bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Pisiform bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Pisiform bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Scaphoid bone.r.001.name: Scaphoid bone
Scaphoid bone.r.001.description: A boat-shaped carpal bone, the largest in the proximal row, on the thumb side of the wrist. It links the two rows of carpal bones.

Trapezium bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Trapezium bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Trapezoid bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Trapezoid bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Triquetrum bone.r.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Triquetrum bone.r.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Axis (C2).001.name: Axis (second cervical vertebra, C2)
Axis (C2).001.description: The second neck vertebra, recognised by a tooth-like upward peg called the dens (odontoid process). The dens sits inside the ring of the atlas, held by the transverse ligament.

Scapula.r.001.name: Scapula
Scapula.r.001.description: A flat, triangular bone on the back of the rib cage. A ridge called the spine crosses its back and ends in the acromion, while the shallow glenoid cavity on its outer angle receives the head of the humerus.

Radius.r.001.name: Radius
Radius.r.001.description: The shorter but thicker of the two forearm bones, lying on the thumb side. Its disc-shaped head turns against the ulna at the elbow, and its broad lower end forms most of the wrist joint with the carpal bones.

Ulna.r.001.name: Ulna
Ulna.r.001.description: The longer, thinner forearm bone on the little-finger side. Its large upper end, with the olecranon and trochlear notch, grips the humerus to form the hinge of the elbow.

Femur.r.001.name: Femur
Femur.r.001.description: The only bone of the thigh and the longest and strongest bone in the body. Its ball-shaped head fits into the acetabulum at the hip, and its two rounded condyles form the upper half of the knee joint.

Hip bone.r.001.name: Hip bone (os coxae)
Hip bone.r.001.description: A large, irregular bone formed by three parts, the ilium, ischium and pubis, which fuse at the cup-shaped acetabulum. The two hip bones, with the sacrum and coccyx, make up the bony pelvis.

Tibia.r.001.name: Tibia
Tibia.r.001.description: The larger, stronger inner bone of the lower leg. Its flat upper surface (tibial plateau) meets the femur at the knee, and its lower end forms the medial malleolus at the ankle.

Fibula.r.001.name: Fibula
Fibula.r.001.description: The thin outer bone of the lower leg, running beside the tibia. It carries little body weight, but its lower end, the lateral malleolus, forms the outer side of the ankle joint.

Sacrum.001.name: Sacrum
Sacrum.001.description: A large triangular bone formed by five fused sacral vertebrae. Its wide upper part joins L5, its sides join the hip bones at the sacroiliac joints, and its tip joins the coccyx.

Temporal bone.l.001.name: Temporal bone
Temporal bone.l.001.description: A complex paired bone at the side and base of the skull made of squamous, mastoid, petrous and tympanic parts. It contains the ear canal, middle ear and inner ear, and has a socket for the lower jaw.

Inferior nasal concha bone.l.001.name: Inferior nasal concha
Inferior nasal concha bone.l.001.description: A thin, curled, scroll-like bone on the side wall of each nasal cavity. Unlike the superior and middle conchae, which belong to the ethmoid, it is a separate facial bone.

Lacrimal bone.l.001.name: Lacrimal bone
Lacrimal bone.l.001.description: A small, thin, fragile paired bone in the inner wall of the eye socket. It holds a groove for the lacrimal sac, part of the tear drainage system.

Nasal bone.l.001.name: Nasal bone
Nasal bone.l.001.description: Two small oblong bones that meet in the midline to form the bony bridge of the nose. The rest of the external nose is shaped by cartilage attached to their lower edges.

Vomer.001.name: Vomer
Vomer.001.description: A thin, flat, unpaired bone in the midline of the nasal cavity. It forms the lower back part of the nasal septum, while the ethmoid's perpendicular plate and the septal cartilage complete the rest.

Maxilla.l.001.name: Maxilla
Maxilla.l.001.description: A paired, pyramid-shaped bone of the midface; the two maxillae fuse to form the upper jaw. It has a hollow body containing the maxillary sinus and four processes: zygomatic, frontal, palatine and alveolar.

Palatine bone.l.001.name: Palatine bone
Palatine bone.l.001.description: A paired, L-shaped bone with horizontal and perpendicular plates. The horizontal plates form the back part of the hard palate, behind the maxillae.

Zygomatic bone.l.001.name: Zygomatic bone
Zygomatic bone.l.001.description: A paired, irregular bone that forms the prominence of the cheek and the outer rim of the eye socket. Its temporal process joins the temporal bone to form the zygomatic arch.

Malleus.l.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Malleus.l.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Incus.l.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Incus.l.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Stapes.l.001.name: Auditory ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes)
Stapes.l.001.description: Three tiny linked bones in each middle ear. The malleus is attached to the eardrum, the incus bridges the gap, and the stapes presses on the oval window of the inner ear.

Upper medial incisor.l.001.name: Incisor teeth
Upper medial incisor.l.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Upper lateral incisor.l.001.name: Incisor teeth
Upper lateral incisor.l.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Upper canine.l.001.name: Canine teeth
Upper canine.l.001.description: Four pointed, cone-shaped teeth, one at each corner of the dental arches. Each has a single, very long root anchored deep in the jaw.

Lower medial incisor.l.001.name: Incisor teeth
Lower medial incisor.l.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Lower lateral incisor.l.001.name: Incisor teeth
Lower lateral incisor.l.001.description: The eight flat, chisel-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, four in each jaw: a central and a lateral incisor on each side. Each has a single root.

Lower canine.l.001.name: Canine teeth
Lower canine.l.001.description: Four pointed, cone-shaped teeth, one at each corner of the dental arches. Each has a single, very long root anchored deep in the jaw.

Upper first premolar.l.001.name: Premolar teeth
Upper first premolar.l.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Upper second premolar.l.001.name: Premolar teeth
Upper second premolar.l.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Upper first molar tooth.l.001.name: Molar teeth
Upper first molar tooth.l.001.description: The large, broad teeth at the back of the mouth, with several cusps and multiple roots: usually three in upper molars and two in lower molars. Adults normally have 12 molars including the wisdom teeth; this model shows the first and second…

Upper second molar tooth.l.001.name: Molar teeth
Upper second molar tooth.l.001.description: The large, broad teeth at the back of the mouth, with several cusps and multiple roots: usually three in upper molars and two in lower molars. Adults normally have 12 molars including the wisdom teeth; this model shows the first and second…

Lower first premolar.l.001.name: Premolar teeth
Lower first premolar.l.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Lower second premolar.l.001.name: Premolar teeth
Lower second premolar.l.001.description: Eight transitional teeth, two on each side of each jaw, with at least two cusps on the chewing surface. Most have one root, though the upper first premolar usually has two.

Lower first molar tooth.l.001.name: Molar teeth
Lower first molar tooth.l.001.description: The large, broad teeth at the back of the mouth, with several cusps and multiple roots: usually three in upper molars and two in lower molars. Adults normally have 12 molars including the wisdom teeth; this model shows the first and second…

Major alar cartilage.l.001.name: Cartilages of nose
Major alar cartilage.l.001.description: The flexible cartilage framework of the lower external nose. The roughly four-sided septal cartilage divides the nostrils, its lateral processes (commonly called the upper lateral cartilages) form the sides of the middle part of the nose…

Lateral process of nasal septal cartilag.name: Cartilages of nose
Lateral process of nasal septal cartilag.description: The flexible cartilage framework of the lower external nose. The roughly four-sided septal cartilage divides the nostrils, its lateral processes (commonly called the upper lateral cartilages) form the sides of the middle part of the nose…

Arytenoid cartilage.l.001.name: Arytenoid and corniculate cartilages
Arytenoid cartilage.l.001.description: A pair of small, three-sided pyramid-shaped cartilages sitting on the back of the cricoid, each capped by a tiny horn-like corniculate cartilage. The vocal cords attach to their forward-pointing vocal processes.

Corniculate cartilage.l.001.name: Arytenoid and corniculate cartilages
Corniculate cartilage.l.001.description: A pair of small, three-sided pyramid-shaped cartilages sitting on the back of the cricoid, each capped by a tiny horn-like corniculate cartilage. The vocal cords attach to their forward-pointing vocal processes.

Fifth rib.l.001.name: True ribs (ribs 1-7)
Fifth rib.l.001.description: The first seven pairs of ribs, each joined directly to the sternum by its own costal cartilage. A typical rib has a head, neck, tubercle and curved body (shaft), with a costal groove underneath for the intercostal nerve and vessels.

First rib.l.001.name: True ribs (ribs 1-7)

Eleventh rib.l.001.name: Floating ribs (ribs 11-12)
Eleventh rib.l.001.description: The last two pairs of ribs, which attach only to the vertebrae at the back and end freely in the muscles of the abdominal wall. Ribs 11 and 12 are the lowest of the false ribs. They are short and have no neck or tubercle.

Twelfth rib.l.001.name: Floating ribs (ribs 11-12)
Twelfth rib.l.001.description: The last two pairs of ribs, which attach only to the vertebrae at the back and end freely in the muscles of the abdominal wall. Ribs 11 and 12 are the lowest of the false ribs. They are short and have no neck or tubercle.

Ninth rib.l.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Ninth rib.l.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Tenth rib.l.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Tenth rib.l.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Costal cartilage of first rib.l.001.name: Costal cartilages
Costal cartilage of first rib.l.001.description: Bars of hyaline cartilage that extend the front ends of the ribs. The first seven join the sternum directly, while those of ribs 8-10 join the cartilage above.

Clavicle.l.001.name: Clavicle
Clavicle.l.001.description: A slender S-shaped long bone, about 15 cm long, that lies horizontally at the base of the neck. Its inner end joins the sternum and its outer end joins the acromion of the scapula.

Humerus.l.001.name: Humerus
Humerus.l.001.description: The long bone of the upper arm. Its rounded head fits into the scapula's glenoid cavity, and its lower end carries the trochlea and capitulum, which meet the ulna and radius at the elbow.

Patella.l.001.name: Patella
Patella.l.001.description: A flat, rounded triangular bone set inside the quadriceps tendon at the front of the knee. Its back surface is covered with thick cartilage where it glides on the femur.

Talus.l.001.name: Talus
Talus.l.001.description: The tarsal bone at the top of the foot skeleton, gripped between the tibia and fibula at the ankle joint and resting on the calcaneus. Much of its surface is covered in joint cartilage.

Calcaneus.l.001.name: Calcaneus
Calcaneus.l.001.description: The largest tarsal bone, forming the heel. Its back part, the calcaneal tuberosity, receives the Achilles tendon, and a shelf on its inner side (sustentaculum tali) supports the talus.

Navicular bone.l.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Navicular bone.l.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Cuboid bone.l.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Cuboid bone.l.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Intermediate cuneiform bone.l.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Intermediate cuneiform bone.l.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Lateral cuneiform bone.l.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Lateral cuneiform bone.l.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

Medial cuneiform bone.l.001.name: Navicular, cuboid and cuneiform bones
Medial cuneiform bone.l.001.description: The five tarsal bones of the midfoot: the boat-shaped navicular on the inner side, the cuboid on the outer side and three wedge-shaped cuneiforms (medial, intermediate, lateral) in front of the navicular.

First metatarsal bone.l.001.name: Metatarsal bones
First metatarsal bone.l.001.description: Five long bones numbered I to V from the big-toe side. Each has a base joining the tarsals, a shaft, and a head that meets a toe.

Sesamoid bones of foot.l.001.description: Small pea-like bones embedded in tendons. In the foot there are usually two under the head of the first metatarsal, inside the tendons of flexor hallucis brevis.

Distal phalanx of first finger of hand.l.name: Phalanges of hand

First metacarpal bone.l.001.description: Five long bones in the palm, numbered I (thumb) to V (little finger). Each has a base joining the carpals, a shaft, and a head that forms a knuckle.

Second metacarpal bone.l.001.name: Metacarpal bones

Capitate bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Capitate bone.l.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Hamate bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Hamate bone.l.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Pisiform bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Pisiform bone.l.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Scaphoid bone.l.001.name: Scaphoid bone
Scaphoid bone.l.001.description: A boat-shaped carpal bone, the largest in the proximal row, on the thumb side of the wrist. It links the two rows of carpal bones.

Trapezium bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)
Trapezium bone.l.001.description: Together with the scaphoid, these seven small bones make up the eight carpals of the wrist, arranged in a proximal row (scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform) and a distal row (trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate).

Trapezoid bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)

Triquetrum bone.l.001.name: Carpal bones (lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate)

Scapula.l.001.name: Scapula
Scapula.l.001.description: A flat, triangular bone on the back of the rib cage. A ridge called the spine crosses its back and ends in the acromion, while the shallow glenoid cavity on its outer angle receives the head of the humerus.

Radius.l.001.name: Radius
Radius.l.001.description: The shorter but thicker of the two forearm bones, lying on the thumb side. Its disc-shaped head turns against the ulna at the elbow, and its broad lower end forms most of the wrist joint with the carpal bones.

Ulna.l.001.name: Ulna
Ulna.l.001.description: The longer, thinner forearm bone on the little-finger side. Its large upper end, with the olecranon and trochlear notch, grips the humerus to form the hinge of the elbow.

Femur.l.001.name: Femur
Femur.l.001.description: The only bone of the thigh and the longest and strongest bone in the body. Its ball-shaped head fits into the acetabulum at the hip, and its two rounded condyles form the upper half of the knee joint.

Hip bone.l.001.name: Hip bone (os coxae)
Hip bone.l.001.description: A large, irregular bone formed by three parts, the ilium, ischium and pubis, which fuse at the cup-shaped acetabulum. The two hip bones, with the sacrum and coccyx, make up the bony pelvis.

Tibia.l.001.name: Tibia
Tibia.l.001.description: The larger, stronger inner bone of the lower leg. Its flat upper surface (tibial plateau) meets the femur at the knee, and its lower end forms the medial malleolus at the ankle.

Fibula.l.001.name: Fibula
Fibula.l.001.description: The thin outer bone of the lower leg, running beside the tibia. It carries little body weight, but its lower end, the lateral malleolus, forms the outer side of the ankle joint.

Eighth rib.l.001.name: Vertebrochondral ribs (ribs 8-10; upper false ribs)
Eighth rib.l.001.description: Ribs 8-12 are called false ribs because they do not reach the sternum by their own cartilage. Ribs 8, 9 and 10 (vertebrochondral ribs) join the cartilage of the rib above, together forming the lower rib margin (costal margin).

Small saphenous vein.r.001.description: The small saphenous vein begins at the outer side of the foot, passes behind the lateral malleolus, and runs up the back of the calf. Near the knee it passes between the two heads of gastrocnemius and usually drains into the popliteal vein.

Popliteal vein.r.001.name: Popliteal vein
Popliteal vein.r.001.description: The popliteal vein forms below the knee where the anterior and posterior tibial veins meet. It rises through the back of the knee alongside the popliteal artery and passes through the adductor hiatus to become the femoral vein.

Posterior intercavernous sinus.001.name: Cavernous sinus
Posterior intercavernous sinus.001.description: The cavernous sinuses are paired venous spaces on each side of the sella turcica and pituitary gland, joined across the midline by intercavernous sinuses. The internal carotid artery and several cranial nerves pass through or along them.
